From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

Review the Seller's documents against the buyer's interests. For EACH of these issues, state the Seller's position, what the buyer should want, and your recommendation with a one-line reason:

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics, AUD 24,000,000, debt-free/cash-free, NSW law

## Headline

The Seller's package would leave the Buyer exposed on almost every known risk. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its cover note on several points:

* **Bluefen:** the cover note says it is "addressed". The letter says no consent has been obtained (DL §2).
* **Riverlark:** the facility has not been repaid (DL §3).
* **Bonuses:** they are not in the funds flow (DL §5).
* **Export incident:** the investigation is "preliminary" (DL §6).

Three problems compound one another:

1. General disclosure of the data room.
2. A constructive-knowledge bar on claims.
3. A single limitation regime for "all Claims of any nature", with no fraud carve-out.

Together these would let the Seller disclose known problems away and then cap or time-bar whatever is left. Every known issue should sit in a **specific indemnity or price mechanism**, outside the general warranty regime.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** A higher cap (AUD 8.4m–12m, i.e. 35–50%). It must apply only to general warranties, not to title, capacity, tax, specific indemnities or fraud.
- **Recommendation:** **Counter** at 50% and settle no lower than about 30%. If W&I insurance is placed, consider accepting a lower Seller cap with the policy sitting above it. *Reason: 20% is low given known, unquantified exposures (privacy, IP, a customer providing 30% of revenue).*

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket (about 1.04% of price), with only the excess recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** About AUD 10k de minimis, with related or series claims aggregated. Basket of about AUD 120k (0.5%) as a **tipping** basket, so recovery runs from the first dollar once it is exceeded. Neither threshold should apply to fundamental, tax, indemnity or fraud claims.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted and counter.** *Reason: an excess-only basket at about 1% is Seller-favourable, and without aggregation, related small losses fall away entirely.*

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months from Completion. The Seller also proposes that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months for general warranties, so the period covers two full audit cycles. Separate, longer periods for title, tax and indemnities (see N-004, N-014, N-016).
- **Recommendation:** **Counter at 24 months and reject the default-to-all language.** *Reason: 18 months may cover only one audit, and the default language silently time-bars every other category.*

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties take the same cap and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Fundamental warranties capped at 100% of price. A time limit of at least 6 years, matching the NSW *Limitation Act 1969* contract period, or 12 years if the SPA is executed as a deed. No thresholds, and no disclosure against them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** *Reason: title is the thing being bought, so a defect means the price is lost. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to cap it at 20%.*

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Under clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5, the limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to "all Claims of any nature". There is no fraud carve-out.
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out from all limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance for fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct or wilful concealment by the Seller, its officers or Company management. Statutory rights, including under ACL s18 / s236, should be preserved for those cases.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. This is a must-have.** *Reason: no buyer should accept a cap on fraud. Courts may not enforce such a cap anyway, but the drafting must not invite that argument.*

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room as at 22 Sept 2026, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL §1.1–1.2).
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosures only. Each must be fairly disclosed with enough detail for the Buyer to identify its nature, scope and financial effect. Further:
  - No general disclosure of the data room or public records.
  - No disclosure against fundamental or tax warranties, or against indemnities.
  - Any data room reference must be to an agreed, archived copy on USB.
  - The data room is now about six weeks stale, so any updated disclosure at signing or Completion should give the Buyer a walk-away right or a claim, not a cure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject general disclosure.** *Reason: combined with N-007, it would wipe out the warranties for anything the Seller placed anywhere in the data room.*

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** No claim for any matter the Buyer *or its advisers* knew about, "including any matter discoverable" from the data room or public records (clause 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An express statement that the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge or investigation (pro-sandbagging). At most, a fallback excluding claims for matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter itself.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** *Reason: constructive knowledge ("discoverable"), extended to advisers, is extreme. It would convert due diligence into a waiver of claims.*

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** "Addressed". The Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the condition as satisfied once the counterparty's written consent is delivered. The Disclosure Letter (§2) confirms there is no consent yet and no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent, waivable only by the Buyer, requiring unconditional written consent under clause 11.2 in a form satisfactory to the Buyer.
  - All clause 11.3 conditions satisfied, with no adverse amendment to commercial terms.
  - The Seller to use "all reasonable" or best endeavours.
  - A sunset date with a termination right.
  - Ideally, protection if Bluefen terminates or materially reduces volume within 12 months (price adjustment, earn-out or escrow).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as drafted.** *Reason: the customer provides about 30% of revenue (AUD 3.6m), and bare delivery of a consent letter does not address the clause 11.3 conditions.*

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** About AUD 3.2m outstanding, with a release "to be provided following Completion". The Disclosure Letter (§3) confirms there is no repayment and no discharge.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Repayment **at Completion** out of the purchase price, against a payoff letter.
  - Executed deeds of release.
  - PPSR financing change statements, or an undertaking to lodge them within 1–2 business days.
  - A release of any security over the shares.
  - The amount treated as Debt and deducted from the price.
  - Confirmation that the change-control trigger in clause 8.1 does not cause a default before payout.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject.** *Reason: the deal is debt-free/cash-free. A post-Completion release leaves the Buyer owning a secured, possibly defaulted borrower.*

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** The AUD 420k (DD-005) is "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised in the funds flow. On-costs are unaddressed (DL §5).
- **Buyer wants:**
  - The AUD 420k plus all on-costs (NSW payroll tax, superannuation where the bonus counts as OTE, PAYG withholding, workers' compensation) treated as Transaction Costs or Debt and deducted from the price.
  - Payment through the Company's payroll, funded by the Seller.
  - A specific indemnity for any shortfall, including amounts that fall due after Completion under the continued-employment conditions.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Itemise and deduct.** *Reason: the Company, which the Buyer will then own, is the employer and will bear the liability. "A matter for the Seller" means nothing unless the price is adjusted.*

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** The existing indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment of AUD 180k and is "adequate".
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Ideally, as a CP or Completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment of every SOW3 fee, plus a confirmatory IP assignment deed from Ironquay (DD-004 clause 7.3).
  - Failing that, a specific indemnity covering all Loss from the Company not owning the SOW3 Project Materials. That includes third-party infringement claims, injunctions, re-development and remediation costs, and customer claims.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap and thresholds, run for at least 4–6 years, and be backed by a retention or escrow.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject as inadequate.** *Reason: the risk is ownership of core IP, not a AUD 180k debt. DL §4 itself admits there is no proof of payment and no assignment.*

### SPA-N-012: Export / privacy incident
- **Seller:** A "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. DL §6 says scope, unauthorised access and notifiability are all unresolved, for about 1,240 records.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: a completed forensic investigation and a documented assessment under the Privacy Act NDB scheme, with Buyer consultation. The 30-day assessment window under s26WH may already have passed, so this needs urgent confirmation.
  - Recovery or deletion confirmation from the unintended recipient.
  - A specific indemnity covering OAIC action and penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims (including Bluefen) and class or representative claims. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, and be backed by a retention.
  - A privacy and data warranty brought down at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the characterisation.** *Reason: the Seller cannot call the incident immaterial while admitting it does not know the facts. Privacy Act penalty exposure is significant.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies and confirmation of the timing, term, terminability, whether amounts are accrued or prepaid, and whether Sandbar is related to the Seller (DL §8 calls them "related").
  - Confirmation that they were not split to sit under an approval threshold.
  - If they were entered in the interim period, confirmation they complied with the conduct-of-business covenants.
  - If any are not genuinely ordinary course or benefit the Seller group, treatment as Leakage or Debt, or termination at the Seller's cost.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet. Diligence first, then price or indemnity.** *Reason: three identical related renewals that must be "read together" suggest splitting, and the Seller's own letter declines to confirm they are ordinary course.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime. "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (clauses 12.3/13), and limitations apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes, each with its own terms:

  | Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds | Disclosure |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | General warranties | 30–50% | 24 months | Yes | Specific only |
  | Fundamental (title, capacity) | 100% | 6–12 years | No | None |
  | Tax | 100% | See N-016 | No | None |
  | Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen as agreed) | Price or uncapped | Bespoke | No | Not qualified |
  | Fraud | Unlimited | None | No | N/A |

  In each case the limitation should apply **only where expressly stated**, reversing the Seller's default.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Reverse the default.** *Reason: this one clause undoes every carve-out the Buyer negotiates elsewhere.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 expressly notes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent checks: an ASIC company extract and history, cross-checked against the register, the constitution, share certificates, issue and transfer resolutions and any shareholder agreement or options.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, particularly for Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Fundamental title warranties (sole legal and beneficial owner, free of Encumbrances, no options or rights to issue) on N-004 terms.
  - Delivery at Completion of signed transfers, certificates and releases.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012 alone.** *Reason: a company-maintained register is not proof of unencumbered title, and the Riverlark security makes encumbrance over the shares a live risk.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers both "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both treated as **open** terms.
  - **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity plus tax warranties, capped at 100% of price, with no thresholds and no disclosure. The time limit should be the later of about 5–7 years or 3 months after the relevant ATO / Revenue NSW amendment period ends, and unlimited for fraud or evasion. Conduct-of-claims provisions are also needed.
  - **IP:** IP warranties at an elevated cap (for example 50–100%) and an extended period (3–4 years), alongside the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled".** *Reason: the Buyer has not agreed these terms. An 18-month, 20% regime is far shorter than the tax amendment periods and is inadequate for a data and analytics business whose value is its IP.*

---

## Other points to note (not in the issue list)
- **DL §1.4 (non-admission):** acceptable only if it does not dilute specific indemnities.
- **DL §7 (lease) and §9 (Mossvale):** confirm through our own review whether change of control triggers anything. Do not rely on the Seller's characterisation. The notification obligation under the lease should become a Completion deliverable.
- **Format of the response:** suggest replying with a full mark-up plus a short issues list, rather than negotiating these points one at a time.

*The percentage and duration ranges above are typical Buyer opening positions in Australian private M&A. Calibrate them against the deal team's commercial priorities and any W&I insurance structure, and have a supervising NSW practitioner confirm them before sending.*

  - Before Completion: a completed forensic investigation and a documented assessment under the Privacy Act NDB scheme, with Buyer consultation. The 30-day assessment window under s26WH may already have passed, so this needs urgent confirmation.
  - Recovery or deletion confirmation from the unintended recipient.
  - A specific indemnity covering OAIC action and penalties, notification and remediation costs, customer claims (including Bluefen) and class or representative claims. It should sit outside the cap, thresholds and disclosure, and be backed by a retention.
  - A privacy and data warranty brought down at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the characterisation.** *Reason: the Seller cannot call the incident immaterial while admitting it does not know the facts. Privacy Act penalty exposure is significant.*

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110k each (AUD 330k total) are ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Copies and confirmation of the timing, term, terminability, whether amounts are accrued or prepaid, and whether Sandbar is related to the Seller (DL §8 calls them "related").
  - Confirmation that they were not split to sit under an approval threshold.
  - If they were entered in the interim period, confirmation they complied with the conduct-of-business covenants.
  - If any are not genuinely ordinary course or benefit the Seller group, treatment as Leakage or Debt, or termination at the Seller's cost.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept the "ordinary course" label yet. Diligence first, then price or indemnity.** *Reason: three identical related renewals that must be "read together" suggest splitting, and the Seller's own letter declines to confirm they are ordinary course.*

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** One regime. "Any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" (clauses 12.3/13), and limitations apply to all Claims of any nature.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes, each with its own terms:

  | Category | Cap | Time limit | Thresholds | Disclosure |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | General warranties | 30–50% | 24 months | Yes | Specific only |
  | Fundamental (title, capacity) | 100% | 6–12 years | No | None |
  | Tax | 100% | See N-016 | No | None |
  | Specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Bluefen as agreed) | Price or uncapped | Bespoke | No | Not qualified |
  | Fraud | Unlimited | None | No | N/A |

  In each case the limitation should apply **only where expressly stated**, reversing the Seller's default.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject. Reverse the default.** *Reason: this one clause undoes every carve-out the Buyer negotiates elsewhere.*

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title is evidenced by the share register at DD-012. DL §10 expressly notes that the Buyer has not verified it.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Independent checks: an ASIC company extract and history, cross-checked against the register, the constitution, share certificates, issue and transfer resolutions and any shareholder agreement or options.
  - A PPSR search against the Seller and the Company, particularly for Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Fundamental title warranties (sole legal and beneficial owner, free of Encumbrances, no options or rights to issue) on N-004 terms.
  - Delivery at Completion of signed transfers, certificates and releases.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not rely on DD-012 alone.** *Reason: a company-maintained register is not proof of unencumbered title, and the Riverlark security makes encumbrance over the shares a live risk.*

### SPA-N-016: Tax / IP open terms
- **Seller:** Considers both "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Both treated as **open** terms.
  - **Tax:** a separate tax indemnity plus tax warranties, capped at 100% of price, with no thresholds and no disclosure. The time limit should be the later of about 5–7 years or 3 months after the relevant ATO / Revenue NSW amendment period ends, and unlimited for fraud or evasion. Conduct-of-claims provisions are also needed.
  - **IP:** IP warranties at an elevated cap (for example 50–100%) and an extended period (3–4 years), alongside the Ironquay indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled".** *Reason: the Buyer has not agreed these terms. An 18-month, 20% regime is far shorter than the tax amendment periods and is inadequate for a data and analytics business whose value is its IP.*
